title: Mediawiki generates invalid LaTeX
body:
**Explain the problem.**

The wikipedia page for Maxwell's equations contains a table with equations, which when converted to LaTeX throws a bunch of errors:

```
! Package amsmath Error: \begin{align} allowed only in paragraph mode.
```

```
FEATURED_TITLE="Maxwell's_equations"
pandoc --from mediawiki --to latex -s -V papersize=a5 -V geometry:margin=1cm -V mainfont="Liberation Serif" "$FEATURED_TITLE.txt" -o "$FEATURED_TITLE.tex"
lualatex --interaction=nonstopmode "$FEATURED_TITLE.tex"
```

[Maxwell's_equations.txt](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/files/13804331/Maxwell.s_equations.txt)

There are other issues with the output but this is the most breaking one.

**Pandoc version?**

Arch Linux:
```
$ pandoc --version
pandoc 3.1.6
Features: +server +lua
Scripting engine: Lua 5.4
User data directory: /home/pepijn/.local/share/pandoc
Copyright (C) 2006-2023 John MacFarlane. Web: https://pandoc.org
This is free software; see the source for copying conditions. There is no
warranty, not even for merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose.
```
author: pepijndevos

title: Text in `<pre>` lost when converting `<table>` in markdown to other formats
body:
**Explain the problem.** Text inside `
` tags in a markdown `` seems to be lost when converting the file to other formats.

To reproduce, create `table.md`:

```markdown


  
    

      first column
      
second column

    

  


```

Run `pandoc -t plain table.md`.

Expected output:

```
first column
second column
```

Actual output:

```
first column
```

Removing the `
` tags or using other tags results in the correct output.

**Pandoc version?**
3.1.11
author: mohd-akram

title: Support CommonMark-like info strings on fenced code blocks
body:
**Explain the problem.**
The CommonMark and GFM specs support an [info string](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.30/#info-string) in fenced code blocks, the first word of which is typically considered the language, like so:

````
```javascript hl_lines="1"
console.log('hello world');
```
````

These are not interpreted correctly by pandoc. Run `pandoc -t plain code.md`.

Expected:

```
    console.log('hello world');
```

Actual:

```
javascript hl_lines="1" console.log('hello world');
```

**Pandoc version?**
3.1.11
author: mohd-akram

title: Prettier does not indent functions properly along with eslint
body: **Prettier 3.1.0** **eslintrc.json** ```sh { "plugins": ["@typescript-eslint", "react", "@stylistic/js"], "rules": { "no-console": "warn", "no-unused-vars": "warn", "no-duplicate-imports": "error", "@stylistic/js/arrow-spacing": "error", "@stylistic/js/indent": ["error", 4, { "SwitchCase": 1 }], "comma-dangle": ["error", "never"], "@stylistic/js/comma-spacing": ["error", { "before": false, "after": true }], "@stylistic/js/eol-last": ["error", "always"], "@stylistic/js/no-extra-semi": "error", "@stylistic/js/no-multi-spaces": "error", "@stylistic/js/no-multiple-empty-lines": "error", "@stylistic/js/no-trailing-spaces": "error", "@stylistic/js/semi": "error", "@stylistic/js/quotes": ["error", "double"], "@stylistic/js/linebreak-style": ["error", "unix"], "eqeqeq": ["error", "always"], "no-cond-assign": ["error", "always"], "camelcase": "error" }, } ``` **prettierrc.json** ```sh { "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/prettierrc.json", "tabWidth": 4, "printWidth": 100, "semi": true, "useTabs": false, "singleQuote": false, "bracketSpacing": true, "endOfLine": "auto", "arrowParens": "always", "trailingComma": "none" } ``` **Input:** ```jsx export const addCartItem = (product: Product, quantity: number = 1) => async (dispatch: Dispatch, getState: () => RootState) => { const cartData = { product: product, quantity: quantity }; try { dispatch(addCartItemRequest()); await axiosInstance.post(CART_URI, cartData); dispatch(addCartItemSuccess(cartData)); saveItemInStorage(CART_ITEMS, getState().cart.cartItems); } catch (error) { const err = error as ErrorResponse; dispatch(addCartItemFailed(throwErrorResponse(err))); } }; ``` **Output:** ```jsx export const updateCartItem = (productId: bigint, quantity: number) => async (dispatch: Dispatch, getState: () => RootState) => { const updateCartQuantityData = { quantity: quantity }; try { dispatch(updateCartItemRequest()); const { data } = await axiosInstance.patch( CART_BY_ID_URI(productId), updateCartQuantityData ); dispatch(updateCartItemSuccess(data)); saveItemInStorage(CART_ITEMS, getState().cart.cartItems); } catch (error) { const err = error as ErrorResponse; dispatch(updateCartItemFailed(throwErrorResponse(err))); } }; ``` **Expected behavior:** ```jsx export const updateCartItem = (productId: bigint, quantity: number) => async (dispatch: Dispatch, getState: () => RootState) => { const updateCartQuantityData = { quantity: quantity }; try { dispatch(updateCartItemRequest()); const { data } = await axiosInstance.patch( CART_BY_ID_URI(productId), updateCartQuantityData ); dispatch(updateCartItemSuccess(data)); saveItemInStorage(CART_ITEMS, getState().cart.cartItems); } catch (error) { const err = error as ErrorResponse; dispatch(updateCartItemFailed(throwErrorResponse(err))); } }; ``` Is there any config/rule i can apply here so that the function body gets indented properly ?
